name: Perplexity
intro: Perplexity turned an AI answer engine into one of the largest consumer subscription businesses built since ChatGPT. Research estimates put its annualized revenue at roughly $750 million in August 2026, up from about $232 million at the end of 2025. Here is the sourced revenue timeline.

modelTitle: How Subscriptions, API Usage and In-Answer Commerce Stack.
modelParagraphs: The core business is a consumer subscription: a free answer engine that converts heavy users into Pro and Max tiers priced per month. That is a volume game — millions of queries feeding a small but compounding paid conversion rate — and it is why Perplexity's revenue curve looks more like a consumer app than an enterprise SaaS ladder.

On top of that sits an enterprise tier for teams that want sourced answers over internal and licensed content, plus newer commerce and advertising surfaces where a shopping intent inside an answer becomes a transaction. The strategic bet is that answers, not links, become the place purchases start — the same bet that makes agentic checkout infrastructure relevant.

faqs.a: Research estimates put Perplexity at roughly $750 million in annualized revenue as of August 2026, up from about $500 million in April 2026 and $232 million at the end of 2025.
No public figure confirms profitability. Inference and content licensing costs are substantial, and the company has continued to raise capital through 2026.

faqs.q: What Are Perplexity Subscribers Actually Paying For?
faqs.a: Faster models, higher limits and research features inside Pro and Max plans. Around that sit enterprise seats, API usage, and an emerging commerce and advertising layer placed inside answers rather than beside them.

faqs.q: How Fast Did Perplexity Reach $100M ARR?
faqs.a: Roughly 22 months from its first meaningful subscription revenue in 2023 — fast for a consumer product, though slower than coding tools like Cursor and Lovable.

faqs.q: How Does Perplexity's Revenue Compare With OpenAI's?
faqs.a: Not closely. OpenAI is reported in the billions of annualized revenue, so Perplexity at roughly $750 million is a fraction of it — the interesting comparison is growth rate, where Perplexity roughly tripled between the end of 2025 and August 2026.
